title: Integrating Climate Change Into Social Protection Approaches: Developing a Policy Framework for Jordan
content:
This article explores the integration of climate change risks into social protection approaches looking at the case of Jordan. Creating cobenefits between SDGs 1 and 13, climate-sensitive social protection can build the resilience of vulnerable groups and foster mitigation and adaptation behaviors. A climate-sensitive social protection framework for Jordan could integrate adaptive, shock-responsive, and anticipatory measures with incentives, infrastructure and capacity measures, and insurance and finance tools through horizontal and vertical integration of government and nongovernment stakeholders.


ABSTRACT

Social protection can protect vulnerable groups from climate change but remains inadequately designed to address climate risks. This article presents a framework for climate-sensitive social protection mechanisms proposed by Jordanian experts. Conceptually, it makes an argument for integrating shock-responsive with transformative social protection approaches that consider compound, slow-onset risks. Operationally, it proposes horizontal and vertical governance integration among public, private, and civil society stakeholders, coordination among agricultural, infrastructural, and development sectors, and bridging state social protection with humanitarian assistance systems.
